title: I Blew It
content: Meaning/Usage: Used to tell someone that you made a big mistake Explanation: When something blows up, it is destroyed. Therefore, blow up implies in this context means to make a big mistake to damage any opportunities. Because making mistakes are very common, a simple way of saying this was needed so people started saying, "I blew it." "I really thought I was going to get the promotion, but I blew it." "I thought he really liked me but I blew it." "I was trying to surprise her for her birthday, but I blew it." A. "How did your interview go?" B. "Not so good, I was very nervous." A. "Why were you nervous?" B. "I think I might have messed up on a few questions so I think I blew it." Other Common Sentences "I messed up." "I missed my opportunity."

examples.sentence: I really thought I was going to get the promotion, but I blew it.
I thought he really liked me but I blew it.
I was trying to surprise her for her birthday, but I blew it.
Not so good, I was very nervous.
I think I might have messed up on a few questions so I think I blew it.
